quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 (10-Q): revenue $3,766,302 thousand, up 53.7% (same-store +46.3%, acquisitions +7.4%), with demand 'especially strong in the technology sector, particularly for data centers'; technology customers were $2,290,001 thousand, 60.8% of revenue (45.8% a year earlier); mechanical segment $2,582,889 thousand and electrical segment $1,183,413 thousand (31.4%); new construction 76.2% of revenue; operating income $624,570 thousand and net income $489,044 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $3,766,302 thousand (+53.7%); technology 60.8% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog (10-Q): $17.81 billion at September 30, 2026, up 26.7% from $14.06 billion at June 30 and 90.0% year over year (mechanical $12,204,936 thousand, electrical $5,609,906 thousand); the same-store sequential increase of $3.67 billion came mainly from the technology sector at its Texas electrical operation ($1.51 billion), its large Texas modular operation ($978.1 million), one Virginia operation ($583.4 million) and one Texas operation ($505.7 million). About 65-75% of remaining performance obligations is expected to be recognized within 12 months; the company expects supportive conditions, especially for manufacturing and technology customers, to continue for the remainder of 2026 and 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $17.81 billion (+26.7% QoQ, +90.0% YoY); Texas electrical +$1.51 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity investment (10-Q): nine-month purchases of property and equipment were $499,437 thousand (2025: $88,813 thousand), primarily building purchases to support growth in the mechanical segment (Q3 mechanical capex $196,538 thousand); the company expects capital expenditures through the end of 2026 and into 2027 to be higher than in previous years. Nine-month acquisitions included Boys Electrical and a modular company in Texas.
